rationale: Delineate the main finding's blast radius with one confirmation shared by two requesters of different kinds: an earlier remote read from node 2 and a later leader-local read. The leader's ordinary broadcast for the local read confirms both, the local requester's ready-to-read result carries its own context and completes, and the earlier remote requester is answered with the local context and stays at index zero. This isolates the defect to the remote reply branch of handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation rather than to confirmation or completion in general, and it uses the harness file already owned by the tick-driven experiment.

scope.description: One confirmation, two kinds of requester. An earlier remote read from node 2 and a later leader-local read are queued at the real leader of a three-voter in-process group; the leader's own broadcast for the local read confirms both, and the ready-to-read result of the local read plus the reply delivered to node 2 are measured.
assumptions: The voter group is three real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3}; node 1 is leader and each node uses a test-only in-memory ILogDB.
The remote read is registered and forwarded through the real follower path; the local read is issued through the leader peer and enters the same queue with node 1 as its source.
The harness uses the leader's ordinary broadcast for the local read and delivers that heartbeat to node 3 only; no other message is reordered.
excluded: No NodeHost, transport, persistence, restart or snapshot path is exercised.
No proposal or membership change is made while the reads are outstanding.
The run observes reply-context association and pending-read completion only; it does not attempt to establish a stale data value.

experiment.prefix: The harness launches three real Raft peers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and ticks node 1 until its current-term no-op is committed. It registers a node-level pending read on node 2 and forwards it through the real follower path, so the leader queues the remote context first. It then registers a pending read on the leader itself and calls the leader peer's ReadIndex, which queues the local context behind the remote one and broadcasts heartbeats carrying that local context. The harness delivers the heartbeat addressed to node 3 back to the leader, collects the resulting messages, and records the context of the reply addressed to node 2. It feeds the leader's own accumulated ReadyToRead output to a pendingReadIndex registered for the local read and records whether that read completed, then delivers the reply to node 2, feeds node 2's ReadyToRead output and the same applied index to its registry, and records whether the remote read completed.
experiment.requirement: A single confirmation that returns an earlier remote request and a later local request must give each requester a result tagged with its own SystemCtx, and both admitted reads must complete once the confirmed index is applied.
experiment.responsibility: handleLeaderReadIndex queues both requests and broadcasts the local context, handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation builds the local ready-to-read result from each request's own context but builds the remote reply from the confirming heartbeat's context, and the two node-level registries consume those results. The experiment exercises those real handlers and changes only which requester is local.

comparisons.description: The reply delivered to the earlier remote requester must carry the context that requester admitted.
The leader's own admitted read should complete after the confirmed index is applied.
The earlier remote requester's admitted read should also complete after the same confirmed index is applied.

experiment.revision_reason: Add a local-versus-remote case on a single confirmation to show which reply branch strands the earlier request.
